messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info
function.description: Retrieve information about a particular star in the universe. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

information.description: The type of information needed about the star.

message.content:
The largest planet that has been observed and confirmed so far is **HD 100546 b**.  
It orbits the young star HD 100546 (about 320 light‑years away) and has a radius roughly **2.5–3 times that of Jupiter** (≈ 200,000 km). Its mass is estimated at around 10–20 Jupiter masses, making it one of the most massive “planet‑like” bodies detected.

> *Note:* While HD 100546 b is the biggest confirmed planet, astronomers continue to discover increasingly massive exoplanets. Some candidates have even higher masses, but their planetary status is still debated—some may actually be brown dwarfs or low‑mass stars. As of now, HD 100546 b remains the largest confirmed planet in the observable universe.
